title: Manipur and Nagaland Chief Ministers Discuss Peace, Development and NH-2 Connectivity
summary: Manipur CM Yumnam Khemchand Singh and Nagaland CM Neiphiu Rio discuss peace, development, NH-2 connectivity and inter-state cooperation in Imphal.
body:
Manipur Chief Minister Yumnam Khemchand Singh and Nagaland Chief Minister Neiphiu Rio held a meeting in Imphal on Wednesday to discuss peace, development, mutual cooperation and strengthening relations between the two neighbouring states.

The meeting took place at the Chief Minister’s official bungalow in Babupara, Imphal, where both leaders discussed matters of mutual interest, including the need to strengthen inter-state relations and promote greater cooperation.

A key issue discussed was ensuring smooth and uninterrupted vehicular movement along the Imphal–Dimapur National Highway (NH-2), an important road connectivity route linking Manipur with Nagaland and other parts of the Northeast.

Nagaland Chief Minister Neiphiu Rio was accompanied by MLA and Advisor to the Nagaland Chief Minister, Achumbemo Kikon. Manipur Deputy Chief Minister Losii Dikho and Naga People's Front (NPF) State President and MLA Awangbow Newmai also attended the meeting.

During the interaction, Rio invited Yumnam Khemchand Singh to attend the Hornbill Festival 2026, scheduled to be held in Nagaland from December 1 to 10.

Rio arrived in Imphal from New Delhi on Wednesday morning and later departed for Kohima by helicopter in the afternoon.

The meeting comes amid efforts to strengthen cooperation between the two neighbouring states, particularly in matters concerning peace, connectivity, development and regional relations.
author: Mirror Lilong Desk
